settings.title: Settings
settings.summary: Choose the display language, wiki auto-ingest, and member permissions.

choose-workspace.title: Choose a workspace
choose-workspace.body: When you first sign in, a workspace is ready for you. Click the workspace name in the sidebar to switch to another workspace or create a “New workspace”. Documents, wiki, and chats are kept separately in each workspace.

screen-layout.title: Screen layout
screen-layout.body: Use the rail on the far left to move between “Home”, “Graph”, “Skills”, “Logs”, “Notifications”, and “Settings”. Next to it, the sidebar holds your document tree, the open document sits in the middle, and the chat panel for talking with the AI agent is on the right. Drag the edge of the sidebar or chat panel to resize it.

chat-panel-tabs.title: Two tabs in the chat panel
chat-panel-tabs.body: Switch between the “Chat” and “Tasks” tabs at the top of the chat panel. Use “Chat” to ask questions about your wiki, and “Tasks” to have the AI agent edit documents, organize folders, or run skills.

write-note.title: Write a new note
write-note.body: Click “Add note” at the bottom of the sidebar and choose “New note” to open a blank note. Type / in the body to insert headings, lists, checklists, tables, code blocks, math, or images, and select text to apply formatting such as bold or italic. Your writing saves automatically, and you can press Cmd/Ctrl+S to save right away.

upload-files.title: Upload files
upload-files.body: Choose “Add note” › “Upload files” to upload Markdown (.md), txt, or PDF files. For Markdown with images, select the .md file together with its image files (png, jpg, gif, webp) or upload them as a zip so the images come along. You can also drag files onto the sidebar tree.

organize-folders.title: Organize with folders
organize-folders.body: Create a folder with “Add note” › “New folder”. Drag an item onto another folder, or right-click it and choose “Move to folder”. Use “Select multiple” to move or delete several items at once.

edit-permissions.title: Set edit permissions
edit-permissions.body: Right-click a document or folder, open “Permissions”, and choose “Inherit from parent”, “Can edit”, or “View only”. With “View only”, only the document owner and OWNERs can edit, and other members see it as read-only. Only OWNERs can change folder permissions, and only the document owner or an OWNER can change document permissions.

delete-restore.title: Delete and restore
delete-restore.body: Documents removed with “Delete” move to the trash and are kept for 30 days. Open “Settings” › “Trash” and click “Restore” to bring one back. Only the document owner or an OWNER can restore.

convert-pdf.title: Convert a PDF to Markdown
convert-pdf.body: Right-click an uploaded PDF and choose “Convert to Markdown”. Before converting, a notice explains that the converted Markdown may not match the original PDF’s content or layout and may be harder to read. Review it, then start the conversion.

track-conversion.title: Track the conversion
track-conversion.body: While converting, the item shows “Converting” in the tree, and opening the converted document shows how many pages have been brought in. When it finishes, a “PDF conversion complete” notification appears and you can start editing.

converted-under-source.title: Conversions grouped under the source PDF
converted-under-source.body: In the tree, the converted document is grouped under its source PDF and labeled “Source PDF” or “Converted”. Click an item to open the conversion or the original PDF. If garbled pages were replaced with raw PDF text, they’re listed under “PDF conversion result” at the top of the conversion, so check them against the original.

describe-figures.title: Describe figures in PDFs
describe-figures.body: By default, figures in a PDF come in as images only. Turn on “Have AI describe figures in PDFs” in “Settings” › “Workspace settings” to write the contents of charts and diagrams into the document so AI search and answers can use them.

markdown-auto-ingest.title: Markdown is added as soon as you upload it
markdown-auto-ingest.body: When you upload Markdown or txt files, they’re added to the team wiki right away. Auto-ingest applies only to documents from members who have the “Add to wiki” permission in Members. OWNERs can turn it off under “Wiki auto-ingest” in “Workspace settings”.

converted-ingest-prompt.title: PDF conversions ask when you open them
converted-ingest-prompt.body: The first time you open a PDF conversion, a dialog asks “Add this document to the wiki?”. Confirm to add it so it can back up chat answers, or skip it and add it yourself later. If “Also auto-ingest PDF conversions right after converting” is on, conversions are added as soon as they finish, without asking.

choose-ingest.title: Choose documents to add
choose-ingest.body: Go to “Graph” in the rail and click the “Add to wiki” button that appears there to switch the sidebar into selection mode. Select the Markdown documents to add and click “Add to wiki (count)” at the bottom; progress is shown, and new pages join the graph when it finishes. An orange dot on the button means some documents are waiting, and Esc cancels the selection.

wiki-status-labels.title: Wiki status labels
wiki-status-labels.body: Labels next to documents in the tree show their wiki status. “Not in wiki” means it hasn’t been added yet, “Edited” means it changed after being added, and “Failed” means adding it failed. Edits only reach chat answers after you add the document again.

refresh-wiki.title: Refresh the wiki
refresh-wiki.body: Click “Refresh wiki” in the rail on the Graph screen to polish wiki pages and add newly found concepts and links to the graph. When a refresh is available after new documents are added, the button shows an orange dot and a “Refresh the wiki?” notification appears. If you don’t like the result, roll that operation back on the “Logs” screen.

graph-nodes.title: Three kinds of nodes
graph-nodes.body: Click “Graph” in the rail to see your wiki as nodes and links. Nodes come in three kinds: uploaded source documents (Raw), information extracted from them (Source), and connected concepts (Concept). Use the filters to show or hide each kind.

graph-explore.title: Explore the graph
graph-explore.body: Drag nodes to move them, and pan or zoom to look around. Double-click a node to open that page in the document area in the middle; wiki pages also list their connected source documents. If the graph looks out of date, click “Refresh graph”.

edit-wiki-page.title: Edit a wiki page yourself
edit-wiki-page.body: On an open wiki page, click “Edit” to change the body and then “Save”. You need to be an OWNER or have the “Add to wiki” permission, and your change is recorded in “Logs” as a wiki edit.

ask-question.title: Ask a question
ask-question.body: Type your question in the “Chat” tab of the chat panel and send it. The AI works out what you’re asking, searches the wiki, and writes an answer based on what it found. Turn on “Web search” to include information from the web, and choose the model from the input box.

answer-sources.title: Check sources and citations
answer-sources.body: Above the answer, you’ll see how many sources were found along with a card for each source document. Click a card to open the original document with the supporting passage highlighted. Citation marks in the answer take you to the same place, and “Listen” reads the answer aloud.

note-evidence-notice.title: Notes that aren’t in the wiki
note-evidence-notice.body: If the note you have open isn’t in the wiki yet, a notice says chat can’t find its contents. Click “Add to wiki” in the notice to use that note in answers. If you edited it after adding it, click “Apply changes” to update the wiki.

save-chat.title: Save a chat as a document
save-chat.body: Open “Chat options” at the top of the chat panel, choose “Save chat as document”, and pick the Q&A pairs to keep; they’re saved as a source document. Click “Add to wiki” afterward to use it as a source for later questions. Use “New chat” in the same menu to start a separate conversation for each topic.

request-task.title: Request a task
request-task.body: Type what you need in the “Tasks” tab and send it. If a document is open, a “Current document” chip is attached, and if you select text in the body, a “Selection: …” chip limits the task to that part. Type @ to attach other documents or / to pick a skill, and press Esc in the input box to stop a running task.

review-edit-proposals.title: Review proposed edits
review-edit-proposals.body: When you ask for changes to the open document, the AI marks each change in the body as a proposal. Click “Accept” or “Reject” on each one, and only accepted proposals are applied. Proposals you set aside can be picked up again later with “Review again”.

approve-plan.title: Review and approve a plan
approve-plan.body: Requests that organize folders or change several documents arrive first as a plan card marked “Awaiting approval”. Click “Open Preview tab” to check new locations, names, and changes, select the items to apply, then click “Accept and organize”, “Accept and edit”, or “Accept and run”. Click “Reject” if you don’t want it; only the items you approve are saved.

auto-approval.title: Auto-approval
auto-approval.body: If approving every time gets tedious, turn on “Creating, moving, and renaming folders” or “Editing and creating documents” under “AI agent auto-approval” in “Settings” › “AI settings”. Plans with AI review warnings or documents you can’t edit still need your approval. Roll back auto-applied edits on the “Logs” screen, and move unwanted new documents to the trash.

browse-skills.title: Browse skills
browse-skills.body: Click “Skills” in the rail to see the skills you can use. Switch between the “All skills”, “Team skills”, and “Personal skills” tabs, and check each skill’s command, description, scope, and status.

create-skill.title: Create a skill
create-skill.body: Click “Create skill” and fill in the skill type (Document, Folder organization, or Template), command, description, and rules. Click “Write with AI” to have AI polish your rules using any reference documents, and the skill goes through a safety review before it’s saved. Choose “Personal” scope to use it in every workspace, or “Team” to share it in the current workspace.

run-skill.title: Run a skill
run-skill.body: Type / in the “Tasks” tab to pick a skill, or click “Run” on the Skills screen and choose the document or folder to run it on. Document skills are saved after you check a preview, and folder organization skills save only the items you approve.

save-request-as-skill.title: Save a request as a skill
save-request-as-skill.body: In the “Tasks” tab, click “Save this request as a skill” on a request you want to reuse. The skill form is filled in from your request, so adjust what you need and save it.

record-meeting.title: Record a meeting
record-meeting.body: Click the microphone button in the chat panel’s input box and choose “Record a meeting”. While recording, speech is transcribed into the “Transcript”, and clicking the same button again stops the recording. “Voice input” in the same menu types up to 60 seconds of speech into the input box.

upload-recording.title: Upload a recording
upload-recording.body: If you already have a recording, choose “Upload a recording” from the microphone menu. You can upload MP3, M4A, WAV, or WebM files up to 500MB, and long recordings may take a few minutes to transcribe.

create-meeting-notes.title: Create and save meeting notes
create-meeting-notes.body: When the recording is done, click “Create meeting notes” to get notes written by AI. Use “Save as new document” to create a document, or “Add to end of document” to append them to the open document. Click “Regenerate” if you want another version.

past-meetings.title: Revisit past meetings
past-meetings.body: Open “Past meetings” from the microphone menu to reopen earlier meetings and check their transcripts and notes. If the recording was kept, click “Listen to recording” to hear it. Deleting a meeting keeps any notes you saved as documents.

export-from-notion.title: Export from Notion
export-from-notion.body: In Notion, export the pages you want in “Markdown & CSV” format to get a zip file. Upload this zip with “Import from Notion”, not with “Upload files”.

preview-import.title: Preview and start the import
preview-import.body: Choose “Add note” › “Import from Notion” and select the zip to see how many folders, documents, tables (databases), images, and PDFs it contains. Click “Start import” to begin: pages with subpages become a document plus a folder of the same name, and databases become a table document with one document per row. Notion links are reconnected to documents in the app.

after-import.title: Convert and add after importing
after-import.body: Imported documents aren’t added to the wiki right away. When the import finishes, you can choose whether to convert PDFs to Markdown and whether to add documents to the wiki. Click “Do it later” to put it off and convert or add them yourself later.

view-logs.title: View operation logs
view-logs.body: Click “Logs” in the rail to see a record of AI operations run in this workspace. Filter with the “AI edits”, “Wiki ingest”, “Wiki refresh”, “Rollback”, and “Wiki edits” tabs, and select an operation to see what changed in documents and wiki pages.

rollback-operation.title: Undo an operation
rollback-operation.body: Select the operation you want to undo and click “Rollback”; a confirmation dialog shows what will be affected. Rolling back a document edit also removes changes saved after that operation, so read the notice carefully. Undoing operations run by other members requires the “Undo actions” permission.

check-notifications.title: Check notifications
check-notifications.body: Under “Notifications” in the rail, view “Workspace” notifications (such as new members joining) and “Tasks” notifications (ingest, refresh, and rollback results) separately. Click “View details in logs” to open the record for that operation, or “Mark all as read” to clear them at once. Turn the notification cards in the bottom-right corner on or off by type in “Settings” › “Notifications”.

change-language.title: Change the display language
change-language.body: In “Settings” › “Display”, pick Korean or “English” under “Language” and the screen switches without reloading. When you’re signed in, the choice is saved to your account so other devices use the same language. The same screen also lets you change the theme, document font, and animation.

auto-ingest-switches.title: Wiki auto-ingest switches
auto-ingest-switches.body: Under “Wiki auto-ingest” in “Settings” › “Workspace settings”, turn “Auto-ingest Markdown uploads into the wiki” and “Also auto-ingest PDF conversions right after converting” on or off. Adding documents to the wiki incurs LLM costs, and only workspace OWNERs can change these switches.

manage-members.title: Manage members and permissions
manage-members.body: In “Settings” › “Members”, click “Invite members” and enter an email and role to send an invitation. For each member, you can turn the “Add to wiki”, “Refresh wiki”, “Write skills”, “Undo actions”, and “Convert PDFs” permissions on or off. OWNERs have all permissions.
